rules.surface_condition: marker that splits a numeric quantity from its unit (the token immediately before is a number and the token immediately after is a measurement-word like million/percent/meters/kilometers/miles/year/etc.)
rules.blamed_rule: - Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value. Examples of such surface forms: numerals and formatted numbers (e.g., "1,200", "2050"), explicit dates, percentages, currency figures, and short fixed named phrases (e.g., organization names, place names). (Prediction to test: cuts adjacent to numerals/dates often score high.)
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: if the token immediately before the marker is NUM and the token immediately after the marker is a measurement/unit token, lower the predicted band to a low range (target band 10–35) because splitting a numeric from its unit often creates a fragment/contrast that the entailment or single-side quality punishes.

rules.surface_condition: marker immediately after a short named phrase / organisation identifier where the name token sits adjacent to the cut (left_last is a single-word org/id token such as parenthood/service/kv62)
rules.blamed_rule: - Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value. Examples of such surface forms: numerals and formatted numbers (e.g., "1,200", "2050"), explicit dates, percentages, currency figures, and short fixed named phrases (e.g., organization names, place names). (Prediction to test: cuts adjacent to numerals/dates often score high.)
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: remove or sharply reduce the generic upward bias that raises scores solely because an immediate neighbor looks like a short organization/place token. Concretely, if the token immediately before the marker is one of a short named/identifier tokens list (check below), reduce the target band (target band 15–45) unless the opposite side also contains a numeral/date or explicit unit that independently justifies a high score.

summary: The model over-boosts cuts that sit next to numbers or short names. In particular it often rates a split between a numeral and its unit ("1.2 <SEG> million", "240 <SEG> kilometers") too highly despite large contradiction/fragment penalties, and it also elevates cuts adjacent to short named tokens or organisation identifiers. Add targeted down-weighting for those surface patterns so the ordering within sentences favors intact numeric+unit chunks and avoids spuriously high cuts at adjacent name/ID boundaries.
